_about: The machine form of docs/guides/POSITIONING.md, the one positioning source of this repository (SITE-REPRESENTATION rules 1 to 4, tickets 155, 249 and 273). Read by tools/Test-SitePositioning.ps1 and tools/Build-SitePages.ps1; nothing at run time reads it. 'positioning' holds the family sentence, the cross-link blurb and the three components in order, each with its state (shipped | gated: built, and held out of every package by a shipping gate that is shut); 'capabilities' is the register of what the product does, each capability with its state, the release that brought it, its evidence, the surface classes allowed to name it and the words that find it; 'retiredPhrases' the words no published surface may say any more (an old definition, a phrase of a retired model, and every promise marker such as 'in development' - canon invariant 17, owner ruling 2026-10-26); 'profiles' the two install intents and where each is explained; 'availability' the component x channel matrix, every cell with the files that prove it (the gate reads them, so a packaging change that contradicts a cell fails the check until this file and the pages say the new truth); 'gated' the rules for naming the gated component (named as what it does, never linked to a download); 'surfaces' names, per file, the region that lists the components ('scopes': regular expressions, the region is the named group 'region' when there is one, else the whole match) and per component a regular expression that finds its words in that file's language - the gate fails when a region is not found, when a component the surface must name (the first 'names' components) is absent, or when one component's words come after the next one's. 'editions' declares what a visitor can obtain, with the one display name each (owned by docs/guides/PRODUCT_NAMING.md). 'facts' types the language count and the platform floor once; the gate reads their real sources and compares every typed claim in the scanned files with them. A change of the order, of a state or of a value is a change of POSITIONING.md and of this file first, then of every surface.

positioning.lead: Four optional parts: a media and file manager that views and sorts photos and videos with one key and manages files in local folders, on servers and on connected devices; a local sharing service that shares folders over SFTP and connects this PC to an exchange account; scheduled file operations that run copy, move, delete and archive on a timetable, installed together with the Share Manager; and a Media Exchange Server that you run yourself, through which your devices reach each other - start with the manager or with the folder-sharing server, and add the rest only if you want it.

blurb._about: The one-line cross-link description (specification 273 T-0) that a sibling product's page copies verbatim beside a link to this product: at most 80 characters, one per interface language, the product name kept outside it.

components.title: Media and file manager
components.says: The viewer and file manager: fast paging through huge folders of photos and video, one key per file, slideshow and playback; local drives, SFTP and SMB servers and the devices of an exchange account browsed and managed as places.

components.title: Local sharing
components.says: The Share Manager and its SFTP worker: the folders you pick open on an Android phone, another copy of the program or any SFTP client; this PC joins an exchange account. Optional, off until switched on.

capabilities.title: FileDO virtual disks
capabilities.says: Hosting FileDO .fdd virtual disks through the same worker. A capability of sharing, off until a disk is registered.

components.title: Scheduled file operations
components.says: Copy, move, delete and archive on a timetable, run by the Share Manager while it runs in your signed-in session and managed in their own scheduling window and the settings page. Installed together with the Share Manager - the same component payload, no separate download and no Windows service.

components.title: Media Exchange Server
components.says: A separate server you run yourself: your devices enroll into an account you create on it and reach each other through it when they cannot reach each other directly. Not folder sharing; neither the manager nor local sharing needs it. Its shipping gate is shut, so no package carries it (the availability matrix says 'not in this package').

capabilities._about: The capability register of specification 273 T-1: what the product does, one row per capability, typed once. 'state' is one of 'states' (the state in the source tree and the published tags, not a promise); 'since' is the CHANGELOG version heading of the first published release that carries it (required when released); 'evidence' names the files or tickets that prove the row (a path is checked to exist); 'surfaces' lists the surface classes of specification 273 section 4 allowed to name it; 'names' finds the capability in English, Russian and Ukrainian text; 'mustName' lists the coverage sets whose every file must name it (so flipping a capability to released makes the gate list exactly the surfaces that still lack it); a 'planned' capability may name only class A and carries 'plannedClaims', the sentences that would promise it, which must match no published surface in en, ru or uk outside an allowed context.

states.released: a published release carries it (the CHANGELOG section of a published tag)
states.built: in the source tree, in no published release yet
states.gated: built, and held out of every package or offer by a switch that is shut
states.planned: nothing in the source tree; tickets only

items.label: View and sort photos and videos with one key per file: slideshow, playback, audio screen, archives as folders, editor, animation to video, JXL, OCR and translation overlay
SFTP servers and SMB shares with a login opened like folders
File manager mode of the Grid panel (F3): local drives, SFTP and SMB resources and exchange devices as places, queued file operations (64-bit program)

Documents in the sorting loop: text shown as text, PDF pages, the cover of an EPUB, any other file as a card
Reading documents, e-books and texts (reflow, bookmarks, table of contents, search)

Optional full PDF and EPUB reader in the 64-bit viewer: pages and layouts, outline, search, bookmarks and installed-voice read aloud, each format off until switched on; the shipped document previews are unchanged

Optional HTML page viewer in the 64-bit viewer: local .html/.htm pages through a restricted WebView2 host (no page script, no remote resources), off until switched on; online pages are a second opt-in (read-only, origins approved by the user)

Optional full text reader and editor in the 64-bit viewer: paged reading of large files, themes, line numbers, search, Markdown view, chosen encodings, atomic saves with backups and encrypted drafts, a selection, the editor's text or the saved file sent to doc-html-translate as a copy, reading, editing and translation each off until switched on; the shipped text preview is unchanged

A scheduled operation that overwrites the free space of a local drive or folder with FileDO's fill and deletes what it wrote: chunk sizes 500/1000/2000/5000 MB, FileDO's reserve kept on the system volume, a stop that lets FileDO clean up, and a run-owned work folder that is removed after every run
Local SFTP folder sharing, QR pairing for Android, phone code intake, FileDO disk hosting (FileDO since 26.10.25.1830)

Scheduled file operations (copy, move, delete, archive on a timetable) in their own scheduling window and the Share Manager settings page; a viewer command with an assignable shortcut and the folder action with source prefill; installed together with the Share Manager
Server edition: the folder-sharing service as a Windows service, its own installer and winget package
Live broadcast of a screen, a window, a camera, a microphone or system audio from the Share Manager, opened in the viewer
Exchange account: this PC joins an account on an exchange server; the account's devices as places, the server clipboard, end-to-end encryption
Guest invitations and password links of an exchange account

A settings standard of an exchange account: the 64-bit viewer saves the chosen groups of its settings on the exchange server and reads them back, local-only values (paths, passwords, keys, window sizes) never leave the computer, and the server keeps one standard per account and program
The Media Exchange Server run by the user: accounts, devices, invitations and registration, limits, service management, remote administration in the browser

Google Drive channel: the settings page and queue, the clipboard, the scheduled sides and the viewer's device folders ship, but no release build carries an OAuth client until the owner registers one, so sign-in cannot succeed

retiredPhrases._about: Words no published surface of this repository may say any more (specification 273 T-1 check b): an old definition of the product, a phrase of a retired model, and every promise marker - 'in development', 'not released yet', 'coming soon' and their translations (canon invariant 17; owner ruling 2026-10-26). Matched case-insensitively over 'scan'; a path in 'allow' is history or a render of history and is skipped, with its reason - unless the entry carries a 'phrases' array, which narrows it: the path is still scanned (retired phrases and planned claims) and only the listed phrases are exempt there. The same scan carries the 'plannedClaims' of the capability register.

availability._about: The component x channel matrix of docs/guides/POSITIONING.md section 4.1, rendered into server.html (region gen:matrix) by tools/Build-SitePages.ps1 and held to the packaging by tools/Test-SitePositioning.ps1. It describes the packages as DEFINED in this source tree (the installer scripts, the winget manifests, the MSIX manifest and packager, the release workflow); what the Releases page offers today is the latest published release, and What's new says which version brought each part. A cell is [state, evidenceId..]; every evidence pattern must match its file, so a packaging change that contradicts a cell fails the check. 'winget' is not a channel of its own: it downloads the same setup.exe as the Releases page, and its silent install takes the first installer type, 'full' - the same default as the wizard. The Microsoft Store has no unattended hosting: a Store package cannot register a Windows service.

gated._about: A component whose state is 'gated' is built and named wherever the components are listed, as what it does, in the present tense, with no promise marker (retiredPhrases; owner ruling 2026-10-26). Its shipping gate is shut, so no package carries it: the availability matrix holds every cell of it 'absent', a mention of it is never inside a link to a download, an installer, a release asset, a store or a winget command, no sentence tells the reader to download or install it, and its door on the landing carries no call to action.

discoverability._about: The machine form of docs/guides/POSITIONING.md section 7 (the worksheet's derived field table, ticket 207 T-1; canon PROMOTION section 2). Every discoverability field of a channel is derived from this block, so a channel never drifts from another: GitHub description and topics, winget Tags, Store search terms, the page titles and the social card. 'applied' names the channels whose fields tools/Test-SitePositioning.ps1 holds against the tree today; a channel joins it in the step that writes its fields (winget and the Store at T-8). Competitor names are never written here: the gate reads them from the internal research guide named in 'competitorTermsSource' (owner decision 2026-10-09, D-7).
